description: GHEtool is the Python package for geothermal borefield sizing developed by KU Leuven, boydens engineering and FH Aachen, now maintained by Enead. It combines ground-response functions with borehole, pipe, fluid and building-load definitions. Inputs include ground layers and temperatures, heat-pump efficiencies and monthly or hourly loads; outputs include borefield size and temperature evolution. Geographic coverage is the selected site, with single-year repeated or explicit multiyear demand scenarios. Source is free under BSD-3-Clause. A limitation is that results depend on ground and load assumptions, and the separate community GUI has no official support. The commercial cloud interface has separate terms. The package supports building heating and cooling infrastructure design. GOLEM (model-golem-geothermal) provides related deeper reservoir modelling. The README contains examples and cites a 2022 JOSS paper; no local borefield was sized.
